newsitem.title: POLAND: New Polish minister sees state's role in economy.
newsitem.headline: New Polish minister sees state's role in economy.

text.p: Poland's new Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz vowed on Tuesday to generally continue his predecesor's privatisation policy but suggested that limiting the number of state-owned firms would not be his priority.
"My assesment of (privatisation) is generally positive though certain correction cannot be ruled out," Pietrewicz told a parliamentary privatisation committee.
"Afer more analyses we may put more stress on certain methods of privatisation and less on others," Pietrewicz added without elaborating. @

Pietrewiucz was put in charge of the new powerful treasury portfolio, which replaced the privatisation ministry on October 1. He took over the top privatisation post from reformist Wieslaw Kaczmarek, who stayed on as deputy minister.
Pietrewicz made clear that reducing the number of state-owned firms would not be his priority.
"Privatisation is to serve the purpose of increasing the Polish economy's efficiency..., and limiting state-owned assets itself does not have to bring effects," he said. @

But he pledged to continue about 50 major privatisation projects initiated by Kaczmarek and vowed to go ahead with the mass privatisation programme under which 15 investment funds, given control over 500 state-owned companies, would enter the bourse next year.
Pietrewicz replaced Kaczmarek as the privatisation head as part of a political deal between the two parties in the ruling leftist coalition linked to a reorganisation of ministries.
